```{r}
# Read data. Environment overrides allow reproducible alternative-corpus runs
# without changing the default analysis inputs.
real_csv_path <- Sys.getenv(
  "ICL_PILOT_REAL_CSV",
  unset = "/Users/shamiraventurini/PycharmProjects/ICL-PILOT/phase2/ENNI/measures/severity_features_raw_real.csv"
)
analysis_tag <- Sys.getenv("ICL_PILOT_ANALYSIS_TAG", unset = "")
plot_suffix <- if (nzchar(analysis_tag)) paste0("_", analysis_tag) else ""

real <- read.csv(
  real_csv_path,
  check.names = FALSE
)

syn <- read.csv(
  "/Users/shamiraventurini/PycharmProjects/ICL-PILOT/phase2/generated/measures/severity_features_raw_syn.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

roster <- read.csv(
  "/Users/shamiraventurini/PycharmProjects/ICL-PILOT/configs/generation/colab_generation_package_direct_rotating_multi_age/master_frozen_roster_4_to_7_year_old.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------
# Standardize synthetic pool first
# -----------------------------
syn <- syn %>%
  mutate(
    File_ID = as.character(File_ID),
    pair_id = as.character(pair_id),
    round_id = as.character(round_id),
    Age_Month = as.numeric(`Age(Month)`),
    source = "synthetic",
    clinical_group = case_when(
      comparison_target_group == "TD"  ~ "TD",
      comparison_target_group == "SLI" ~ "SLI",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    age_cohort = case_when(
      Age_Month >= 48 & Age_Month < 60 ~ "4_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 60 & Age_Month < 72 ~ "5_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 72 & Age_Month < 84 ~ "6_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 84 & Age_Month < 96 ~ "7_year_old",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    round_batch = interaction(age_cohort, round_id, drop = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(clinical_group),
    !is.na(age_cohort),
    Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96
  )

# -----------------------------
# Prompt children used in each round
# Source of truth = synthetic metadata
# -----------------------------
prompt_map <- syn %>%
  transmute(
    round_id = as.character(round_id),
    age_cohort = as.character(age_cohort),
    round_batch = interaction(age_cohort, round_id, drop = TRUE),
    prompt_td_child_id = as.character(prompt_td_child_id),
    prompt_sli_child_id = as.character(prompt_sli_child_id)
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(prompt_td_child_id, prompt_sli_child_id),
    names_to = "prompt_group",
    values_to = "child_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(child_id), child_id != "") %>%
  mutate(
    clinical_group = case_when(
      prompt_group == "prompt_td_child_id"  ~ "TD",
      prompt_group == "prompt_sli_child_id" ~ "SLI"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(round_id, age_cohort, round_batch, clinical_group, child_id) %>%
  distinct()

# -----------------------------
# Standardize real pool
# -----------------------------
real <- real %>%
  mutate(
    File_ID = as.character(File_ID),
    Age_Month = as.numeric(`Age(Month)`),
    source = "real",
    pair_id = NA_character_,
    round_id = NA_character_,
    clinical_group = case_when(
      Group == "TD"  ~ "TD",
      Group == "SLI" ~ "SLI",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    comparison_target_group = clinical_group,
    age_cohort = case_when(
      Age_Month >= 48 & Age_Month < 60 ~ "4_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 60 & Age_Month < 72 ~ "5_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 72 & Age_Month < 84 ~ "6_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 84 & Age_Month < 96 ~ "7_year_old",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(clinical_group),
    !is.na(age_cohort),
    Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96
  )

# -----------------------------
# Build fold-stacked held-out evaluation dataframe
# For each age-specific round:
# - real children are included only if they were NOT prompts in that round
# - real children are restricted to the same age cohort
# - synthetic children come from that same age-specific round
# -----------------------------
round_batches <- sort(unique(syn$round_batch))

df_all <- bind_rows(lapply(round_batches, function(rb) {

  syn_r <- syn %>%
    filter(round_batch == rb)

  cohort_r <- unique(syn_r$age_cohort)
  round_id_r <- unique(syn_r$round_id)

  if (length(cohort_r) != 1 || length(round_id_r) != 1) {
    stop(paste("Problem: round_batch", rb, "does not map uniquely to one cohort/round_id"))
  }

  prompt_r <- prompt_map %>%
    filter(round_batch == rb)

  real_r <- real %>%
    filter(age_cohort == cohort_r) %>%
    mutate(
      round_id = round_id_r,
      round_batch = rb
    ) %>%
    anti_join(
      prompt_r,
      by = c("File_ID" = "child_id", "clinical_group")
    )

  bind_rows(real_r, syn_r)
})) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age_Month)) %>%
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = c("real", "synthetic")),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI")),
    age_cohort = factor(
      age_cohort,
      levels = c("4_year_old", "5_year_old", "6_year_old", "7_year_old")
    ),
    population = factor(
      paste(source, clinical_group, sep = "_"),
      levels = c("real_TD", "synthetic_TD", "real_SLI", "synthetic_SLI")
    ),
    source_is_synthetic = if_else(source == "synthetic", 1L, 0L),

    # IMPORTANT: make synthetic cluster_id unique across age cohorts / rounds
    cluster_id = if_else(
      source == "synthetic",
      paste0("synthetic_", age_cohort, "_", round_id, "_", pair_id),
      paste0("real_", File_ID)
    ),

    unit_id = cluster_id,
    Age_c = Age_Month - mean(Age_Month, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Optional subsets
df_td  <- df_all %>% filter(clinical_group == "TD")
df_sli <- df_all %>% filter(clinical_group == "SLI")

# Quick checks
table(df_all$source, df_all$clinical_group)
table(df_all$age_cohort, df_all$source, df_all$clinical_group)
table(df_all$round_batch, df_all$population)
summary(df_all$Age_Month)
```

# Analyses {.tabset}

## PCA {.tabset}


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

# -----------------------------
# 1) Build an independent transcript-level dataset
# -----------------------------
real_unique <- real %>%
  filter(!is.na(clinical_group), Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96) %>%
  distinct(File_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

syn_unique <- syn %>%
  filter(!is.na(clinical_group), Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96) %>%
  distinct(File_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

pca_base <- bind_rows(real_unique, syn_unique) %>%
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = c("real", "synthetic")),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI")),
    source_is_synthetic = if_else(source == "synthetic", 1L, 0L),
    population = factor(
      paste(ifelse(source_is_synthetic == 1, "Synthetic", "Real"), clinical_group),
      levels = c("Real TD", "Synthetic TD", "Real SLI", "Synthetic SLI")
    )
  )

table(pca_base$population)

# -----------------------------
# 2) Exclude metadata / IDs / obvious non-features
# -----------------------------
exclude_vars <- c(
  "bundle_id", "pair_id", "round_id", "round_batch", "replicate_id",
  "source", "stage", "age_cohort",
  "comparison_target_group", "evaluation_pool_policy", "prompt_exclusion_policy",
  "source_child_id", "prompt_td_child_id", "prompt_sli_child_id",
  "td_child_id", "sli_child_id", "sli_age_generated_from",
  "sli_severity_band_generated_from", "sli_profile_label_generated_from",
  "story_slots", "n_stories",
  "File_ID", "File_kideval", "Group", "Sex",
  "Age(Month)", "Age_Month", "Age_c",
  "source_is_synthetic", "clinical_group", "population",
  "cluster_id", "unit_id",
  "#utterances", "#words",
  "DSS_tbl_warning_50",
  "retracing_per_utt",
  "past_overgeneralization_errors",
  "past_verb_opportunities"
  # add "repetition_per_utt" here too if you decide it was not extracted symmetrically
)

feature_df <- pca_base %>%
  select(-any_of(exclude_vars)) %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

cat("Numeric candidate features:", ncol(feature_df), "\n")

# -----------------------------
# 3) Remove features with too much missingness
# -----------------------------
na_prop <- colMeans(is.na(feature_df))
keep_na <- names(na_prop[na_prop <= 0.20])
feature_df <- feature_df %>% select(all_of(keep_na))

cat("Features after missingness filter:", ncol(feature_df), "\n")

# -----------------------------
# 4) Remove near-zero variance features
# -----------------------------
is_nzv <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) <= 1) return(TRUE)
  if (sd(x) < 1e-8) return(TRUE)
  if (length(unique(x)) <= 2 && max(table(x)) / length(x) > 0.95) return(TRUE)
  FALSE
}

nzv_flags <- sapply(feature_df, is_nzv)
feature_df <- feature_df[, !nzv_flags, drop = FALSE]

cat("Features after near-zero variance filter:", ncol(feature_df), "\n")

# -----------------------------
# 5) Remove highly correlated features
# -----------------------------
remove_high_corr <- function(df, cutoff = 0.90) {
  if (ncol(df) < 2) return(df)

  keep <- colnames(df)

  repeat {
    cor_mat <- cor(df[, keep, drop = FALSE], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
    diag(cor_mat) <- 0

    max_cor <- suppressWarnings(max(abs(cor_mat), na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(max_cor) || max_cor < cutoff) break

    idx <- which(abs(cor_mat) == max_cor, arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
    v1 <- colnames(cor_mat)[idx[1]]
    v2 <- colnames(cor_mat)[idx[2]]

    mean1 <- mean(abs(cor_mat[v1, ]), na.rm = TRUE)
    mean2 <- mean(abs(cor_mat[v2, ]), na.rm = TRUE)

    drop_var <- if (mean1 >= mean2) v1 else v2
    keep <- setdiff(keep, drop_var)
  }

  df[, keep, drop = FALSE]
}

feature_df_pruned <- remove_high_corr(feature_df, cutoff = 0.90)

cat("Features after correlation pruning:", ncol(feature_df_pruned), "\n")
print(colnames(feature_df_pruned))

# -----------------------------
# 6) Keep complete cases
# -----------------------------
pca_complete <- bind_cols(
  pca_base %>% select(population, source, clinical_group, Age_Month),
  feature_df_pruned
) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(across(all_of(colnames(feature_df_pruned)))))

cat("Rows entering PCA:", nrow(pca_complete), "\n")
table(pca_complete$population)

# -----------------------------
# 7) Run PCA
# -----------------------------
pca_fit <- prcomp(
  pca_complete %>% select(all_of(colnames(feature_df_pruned))),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)

var_explained <- (pca_fit$sdev^2) / sum(pca_fit$sdev^2)

pca_var_df <- tibble(
  PC = paste0("PC", seq_along(var_explained)),
  variance_explained = var_explained,
  cumulative = cumsum(var_explained)
)

print(pca_var_df)

```
```{r}
# scores
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_fit$x) %>%
  bind_cols(pca_complete %>% select(population, source, clinical_group, Age_Month))

# -----------------------------
# 8) Scree plot
# -----------------------------
ggplot(pca_var_df, aes(x = seq_along(variance_explained), y = variance_explained)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumulative), group = 1, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cumulative), size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(nrow(pca_var_df)), labels = pca_var_df$PC) +
  labs(
    x = "Principal component",
    y = "Variance explained",
    title = "Scree plot"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
```{r}
library(psych)

fa.parallel(
  pca_complete %>% select(all_of(colnames(feature_df_pruned))),
  fa = "pc",
  n.iter = 100,
  show.legend = TRUE,
  main = "Parallel analysis"
)
```
The PCA suggests that the feature space is not one-dimensional. There are about four meaningful latent components, with the first two already explaining more than half of the variance. So the data seem to have a compact but non-trivial internal structure: a strong broad first dimension, a second major contrast, and then two smaller but still meaningful components.


```{r}
# loadings
pca_loadings <- as_tibble(pca_fit$rotation, rownames = "feature")

pca_loadings %>%
  select(feature, PC1, PC2, PC3, PC4) %>%
  mutate(across(c(PC1, PC2, PC3, PC4), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC1))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# PC1
pca_loadings %>%
  select(feature, PC1) %>%
  mutate(PC1 = round(PC1, 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC1))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# PC2
pca_loadings %>%
  select(feature, PC2) %>%
  mutate(PC2 = round(PC2, 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC2))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# PC3
pca_loadings %>%
  select(feature, PC3) %>%
  mutate(PC3 = round(PC3, 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC3))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# PC4
pca_loadings %>%
  select(feature, PC4) %>%
  mutate(PC4 = round(PC4, 3)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC4))) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```
* PC1: syntactic complexity; higher = more syntactically complex speech (> coordination & subordination; longer & deeper structures; > complex NPs; > aux/copulas structures).
* PC2: grammatical maturity; higher = longer, grammatically richer sentences and phrase structures, less word-level errors.
* PC3: error proneness and lexical instability; lower lexical richness.
* PC4: Residual morphosyntactic control; a weaker residual component, roughly contrasting interrogative/irregular-form control with errorful production

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(GGally)

pca_scores_plotly <- as.data.frame(pca_fit$x) %>%
  mutate(
    population = pca_complete$population,
    PC3 = -PC3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Syntax  = PC1,
    Grammar = PC2,
    Errors  = PC3,

  )

GGally::ggpairs(
  pca_scores_plotly,
  columns = c(
    "Syntax",
    "Grammar",
    "Errors",
    "Control"
  ),
  aes(color = population, alpha = 0.7)
)
```
The first two components already separate the populations in a meaningful way, but not perfectly.
Synthetic data are not identical to real data, and synthetic SLI does not sit neatly on top of real SLI.

* PC1-PC2 correlation: real strong positive correlation; synthetic weakly negative correlation.= In the real data, more syntactic complexity tends to go together with more grammatical maturity.
In the synthetic data, that relationship is not preserved in the same way.

```{r}
      color = NULL
    ) +

}
```

## Distributional Distance {.tabset}

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)

# -----------------------------
# Independent transcript-level dataset: ages 4–7
# one row per transcript
# -----------------------------
real_indep <- real %>%
  filter(!is.na(clinical_group), Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96) %>%
  distinct(File_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

syn_indep <- syn %>%
  filter(!is.na(clinical_group), Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96) %>%
  distinct(File_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)

profile_df <- bind_rows(real_indep, syn_indep) %>%
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = c("real", "synthetic")),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI")),
    population = factor(
      paste(ifelse(source == "synthetic", "Synthetic", "Real"), clinical_group),
      levels = c("Real TD", "Synthetic TD", "Real SLI", "Synthetic SLI")
    )
  )

table(profile_df$population)

# Reuse the PCA feature set for distributional comparisons.
main_features <- colnames(feature_df_pruned)
```


```{r}
wasserstein_1d <- function(x, y, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  y <- y[is.finite(y)]
  if (length(x) < 2 || length(y) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  qx <- quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, type = 8)
  qy <- quantile(y, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE, type = 8)
  mean(abs(qx - qy))
}



compare_distribution <- function(df, feature, group_name) {
  real_vals <- df %>%
    filter(source == "real", clinical_group == group_name) %>%
    pull(all_of(feature))

  syn_vals <- df %>%
    filter(source == "synthetic", clinical_group == group_name) %>%
    pull(all_of(feature))

  real_vals <- real_vals[is.finite(real_vals)]
  syn_vals  <- syn_vals[is.finite(syn_vals)]

  if (length(real_vals) < 2 || length(syn_vals) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      feature = feature,
      group = group_name,
      n_real = length(real_vals),
      n_syn = length(syn_vals),
      real_mean = NA_real_,
      syn_mean = NA_real_,
      mean_diff = NA_real_,
      wasserstein = NA_real_,
      ks_D = NA_real_,
      ks_p = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  ks_out <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(real_vals, syn_vals))

  tibble(
    feature = feature,
    group = group_name,
    n_real = length(real_vals),
    n_syn = length(syn_vals),
    real_mean = mean(real_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    syn_mean = mean(syn_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_diff = mean(syn_vals, na.rm = TRUE) - mean(real_vals, na.rm = TRUE),
    wasserstein = wasserstein_1d(real_vals, syn_vals),
    ks_D = unname(ks_out$statistic),
    ks_p = ks_out$p.value
  )
}

dist_results <- map_dfr(main_features, ~ compare_distribution(profile_df, .x, "TD")) %>%
  bind_rows(
    map_dfr(main_features, ~ compare_distribution(profile_df, .x, "SLI"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ks_p_adj = p.adjust(ks_p, method = "BH")
  )

dist_results %>%
  arrange(group, desc(wasserstein))
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)

# standardize each feature using mean/sd from the REAL data of that clinical group
compare_distribution_std <- function(df, feature, group_name) {
  real_vals <- df %>%
    filter(source == "real", clinical_group == group_name) %>%
    pull(all_of(feature))

  syn_vals <- df %>%
    filter(source == "synthetic", clinical_group == group_name) %>%
    pull(all_of(feature))

  real_vals <- real_vals[is.finite(real_vals)]
  syn_vals  <- syn_vals[is.finite(syn_vals)]

  if (length(real_vals) < 2 || length(syn_vals) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      feature = feature,
      group = group_name,
      wasserstein_std = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  mu <- mean(real_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd0 <- sd(real_vals, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (!is.finite(sd0) || sd0 == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      feature = feature,
      group = group_name,
      wasserstein_std = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  real_z <- (real_vals - mu) / sd0
  syn_z  <- (syn_vals  - mu) / sd0

  tibble(
    feature = feature,
    group = group_name,
    wasserstein_std = wasserstein_1d(real_z, syn_z)
  )
}

dist_std_results <- map_dfr(main_features, ~ compare_distribution_std(profile_df, .x, "TD")) %>%
  bind_rows(
    map_dfr(main_features, ~ compare_distribution_std(profile_df, .x, "SLI"))
  )

dist_std_results %>%
  arrange(group, desc(wasserstein_std))
```
Synthetic data are distributionally mismatched from real data in both groups, and the mismatch is especially severe for core syntactic measures.

```{r}
plot_df <- dist_std_results %>%
  group_by(feature) %>%
  mutate(max_w = max(wasserstein_std, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    feature = reorder(feature, max_w)
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = feature, y = wasserstein_std, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.65) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Standardized Wasserstein distance",
    title = "Distributional mismatch: synthetic vs real"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Covariance/correlation preservation {.tabset}

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# -----------------------------
# Use the same feature set that entered the PCA
# -----------------------------
broad_features <- colnames(feature_df_pruned)

# If needed, drop known problematic/asymmetric features here too
broad_features <- setdiff(
  broad_features,
  c("retracing_per_utt")
)
# add "repetition_per_utt" too if you decide it should be excluded:
# broad_features <- setdiff(broad_features, c("retracing_per_utt", "repetition_per_utt"))

# -----------------------------
# Use the independent transcript-level 4–7 dataset
# same one used for PCA
# -----------------------------
corr_base <- pca_complete %>%
  select(population, source, clinical_group, all_of(broad_features))

table(corr_base$population)

# -----------------------------
# Helper functions
# -----------------------------
upper_tri_vec <- function(mat) {
  mat[upper.tri(mat)]
}

get_corr_mat <- function(df, group_name, feature_names) {
  tmp <- df %>%
    filter(clinical_group == group_name) %>%
    select(source, all_of(feature_names))

  real_df <- tmp %>%
    filter(source == "real") %>%
    select(-source)

  syn_df <- tmp %>%
    filter(source == "synthetic") %>%
    select(-source)

  # keep only features with non-zero variance in BOTH real and synthetic
  keep_vars <- intersect(
    names(real_df)[sapply(real_df, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)],
    names(syn_df)[sapply(syn_df, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)]
  )

  real_df <- real_df %>% select(all_of(keep_vars))
  syn_df  <- syn_df  %>% select(all_of(keep_vars))

  list(
    keep_vars = keep_vars,
    real = cor(real_df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
    synthetic = cor(syn_df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  )
}

corr_similarity <- function(cor_real, cor_syn) {
  v1 <- upper_tri_vec(cor_real)
  v2 <- upper_tri_vec(cor_syn)

  tibble(
    corr_of_correlations = cor(v1, v2, use = "complete.obs"),
    mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(v1 - v2), na.rm = TRUE),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(v1 - v2), na.rm = TRUE),
    frobenius = sqrt(sum((cor_real - cor_syn)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
}
```

```{r}
# -----------------------------
# Compute TD and SLI correlation matrices

corr_td_broad  <- get_corr_mat(corr_base, "TD", broad_features)
corr_sli_broad <- get_corr_mat(corr_base, "SLI", broad_features)
```

```{r}
plot_corr_preservation <- function(cor_real, cor_syn, title_text) {
  df_plot <- tibble(
    real = upper_tri_vec(cor_real),
    synthetic = upper_tri_vec(cor_syn)
  )

  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = real, y = synthetic)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.65, size = 2) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      x = "Real correlations",
      y = "Synthetic correlations",
      title = title_text
    ) +
    theme_classic()
}

plot_corr_preservation(

  corr_td_broad$synthetic,
  "TD: correlation preservation"
)

plot_corr_preservation(

  corr_sli_broad$synthetic,

)
```

```{r}
plot_corr_diff <- function(cor_real, cor_syn, title_text) {
  diff_mat <- cor_syn - cor_real

  as.data.frame(diff_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("feature1") %>%
    pivot_longer(-feature1, names_to = "feature2", values_to = "diff") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = feature1, y = feature2, fill = diff)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#2166ac",
      mid = "white",
      high = "#b2182b",
      midpoint = 0
    ) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      fill = "Syn - Real r",
      title = title_text
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)
    )
}

plot_corr_diff(
  corr_td_broad$real,
  corr_td_broad$synthetic,
  "TD: correlation differences"
)

plot_corr_diff(
  corr_sli_broad$real,
  corr_sli_broad$synthetic,
  "SLI: correlation differences"
)
```
RED = synthetic correlation > real
BLUE = synthetic correlation < real

The synthetic data do not just shift feature values; they change the architecture of the profile.

```{r}
top_corr_diffs <- function(cor_real, cor_syn, top_n = 15) {
  diff_mat <- cor_syn - cor_real
  abs_diff_mat <- abs(diff_mat)

  as.data.frame(abs_diff_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("feature1") %>%
    pivot_longer(-feature1, names_to = "feature2", values_to = "abs_diff") %>%
    mutate(signed_diff = as.vector(diff_mat)) %>%
    filter(feature1 != feature2) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(pair = paste(sort(c(feature1, feature2)), collapse = " -- ")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    distinct(pair, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    arrange(desc(abs_diff)) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_n) %>%
    select(pair, abs_diff, signed_diff)
}

top_td_broad  <- top_corr_diffs(corr_td_broad$real,  corr_td_broad$synthetic, top_n = 15)
top_sli_broad <- top_corr_diffs(corr_sli_broad$real, corr_sli_broad$synthetic, top_n = 15)

top_td_broad
```

```{r}

```
Synthetic transcript have higher mlu than real ones. SLI lower than TD. Magnitude of difference is the same between synthetic SLI and TD. mlu increases with age. clear inflation in synthetic SLI

* Intercept = predicted mlu for real TD in round 1 at mean age (centered)
* source_is_synthetic = TD synthetic data are about 5.5 morphemes higher
* clinical_groupSLI = real SLI is 1.36 morphemes lower
* Age_c = mlu increases with age
* source_is_synthetic:clinical_groupSLI = synthetic boost is higher in SLI
* source_is_synthetic:Age_c = Synthetic data show a somewhat flatter age slope than real data, but this is only marginal.
* clinical_groupSLI:Age_c = SLI shows steeper age-related increase than TD

calculates the diversity of a text by modelling how the Type-Token Ratio (TTR) changes as sample sizes increase.

is age linear or quadratic?

```{r}

```
In the real data, SLI has lower lexical diversity than TD. In the synthetic data, lexical diversity is inflated for both groups, but especially for SLI, so the real TD–SLI difference is greatly reduced or effectively erased.

* Intercept = predicted lexical diversity for real TD in round 1 at mean age (centered)
* source_is_synthetic = TD synthetic data have a much higher lexical diversity than real transcripts.
* clinical_groupSLI = real SLI is 5.4 points lower than TD
* Age_c = lexical diversity increases with age
* source_is_synthetic:clinical_groupSLI = the synthetic-real difference is even larger in SLI than in TD.

Synthetic transcripts have lower DSS than real ones. SLI < TD. DSS increases with age. synthetic vs real gap smaller in SLI than TD (only marginally significant). The synthetic data do not erase the clinical-group difference; they preserve it fairly well.

* Intercept = Predicted DSS for real TD at mean age.
* source_is_synthetic = In the TD group, synthetic transcripts are about 0.54 DSS points lower than real transcripts.
* clinical_groupSLI = Among real transcripts, SLI is about 1.65 DSS points lower than TD.
* Age_c = DSS increases of 0.03 points per months.
* source_is_synthetic:clinical_groupSLI = This suggests the synthetic penalty is more positive in SLI than in TD.

### Productive Morphology {.tabset}
#### past over-generalisation

Overgeneralization is primarily a developmental phenomenon tied to productive morphology. These errors appear after acquisition of regular past tense is completed. In SLI/DLD, the better-established clinical pattern is reduced tense marking and increased zero-marking, not necessarily increased overgeneralization. They lag behind past acquisition therefore, they do not yet showcase this error pattern.

Given a past-tense opportunity, what is the probability of producing an overgeneralized past form?

```{r}
# -----------------------------
# Read DEV data
# -----------------------------
real_dev <- read.csv(
  "/Users/shamiraventurini/PycharmProjects/ICL-PILOT/phase2/ENNI/measures/dev_measures.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

syn_dev <- read.csv(
  "/Users/shamiraventurini/PycharmProjects/ICL-PILOT/phase2/generated/measures/dev_measures.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------
# Build prompt map from synthetic metadata
# If 'syn' already exists in memory from the main feature pipeline, use it.
# Otherwise use syn_dev if it contains the prompt columns.
# -----------------------------
prompt_source <- if (exists("syn")) syn else syn_dev

prompt_source <- prompt_source %>%
  mutate(
    round_id = as.character(round_id),
    Age_Month = as.numeric(`Age(Month)`),
    age_cohort = case_when(
      Age_Month >= 48 & Age_Month < 60 ~ "4_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 60 & Age_Month < 72 ~ "5_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 72 & Age_Month < 84 ~ "6_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 84 & Age_Month < 96 ~ "7_year_old",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    round_batch = interaction(age_cohort, round_id, drop = TRUE)
  )

prompt_map <- prompt_source %>%
  transmute(
    round_id = as.character(round_id),
    age_cohort = as.character(age_cohort),
    round_batch = interaction(age_cohort, round_id, drop = TRUE),
    prompt_td_child_id = as.character(prompt_td_child_id),
    prompt_sli_child_id = as.character(prompt_sli_child_id)
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(prompt_td_child_id, prompt_sli_child_id),
    names_to = "prompt_group",
    values_to = "child_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(child_id), child_id != "") %>%
  mutate(
    clinical_group = case_when(
      prompt_group == "prompt_td_child_id"  ~ "TD",
      prompt_group == "prompt_sli_child_id" ~ "SLI"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(round_id, age_cohort, round_batch, clinical_group, child_id) %>%
  distinct()

# -----------------------------
# Real DEV pool: ages 4–7
# -----------------------------
real_dev_4to7 <- real_dev %>%
  mutate(
    File_ID = as.character(File_ID),
    Age_Month = as.numeric(`Age(Month)`),
    source = "real",
    pair_id = NA_character_,
    round_id = NA_character_,
    clinical_group = case_when(
      Group == "TD"  ~ "TD",
      Group == "SLI" ~ "SLI",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    age_cohort = case_when(
      Age_Month >= 48 & Age_Month < 60 ~ "4_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 60 & Age_Month < 72 ~ "5_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 72 & Age_Month < 84 ~ "6_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 84 & Age_Month < 96 ~ "7_year_old",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(clinical_group),
    !is.na(age_cohort),
    Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96
  )

# -----------------------------
# Synthetic DEV pool: ages 4–7
# -----------------------------
syn_dev_4to7 <- syn_dev %>%
  mutate(
    File_ID = as.character(File_ID),
    pair_id = as.character(pair_id),
    round_id = as.character(round_id),
    Age_Month = as.numeric(`Age(Month)`),
    source = "synthetic",
    clinical_group = case_when(
      comparison_target_group == "TD"  ~ "TD",
      comparison_target_group == "SLI" ~ "SLI",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    age_cohort = case_when(
      Age_Month >= 48 & Age_Month < 60 ~ "4_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 60 & Age_Month < 72 ~ "5_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 72 & Age_Month < 84 ~ "6_year_old",
      Age_Month >= 84 & Age_Month < 96 ~ "7_year_old",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    round_batch = interaction(age_cohort, round_id, drop = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(clinical_group),
    !is.na(age_cohort),
    Age_Month >= 48, Age_Month < 96
  )

# -----------------------------
# Build fold-stacked held-out DEV dataframe
# Stack by age-specific round_batch
# -----------------------------
round_batches <- sort(unique(syn_dev_4to7$round_batch))


df_dev_all <- bind_rows(lapply(round_batches, function(rb) {

  syn_r <- syn_dev_4to7 %>%
    filter(round_batch == rb)

  cohort_r <- unique(syn_r$age_cohort)
  round_id_r <- unique(syn_r$round_id)

  if (length(cohort_r) != 1 || length(round_id_r) != 1) {
    stop(paste("Problem: round_batch", rb, "does not map uniquely to one cohort/round_id"))
  }

  prompt_r <- prompt_map %>%
    filter(round_batch == rb)

  real_r <- real_dev_4to7 %>%
    filter(age_cohort == cohort_r) %>%
    mutate(
      round_id = round_id_r,
      round_batch = rb
    ) %>%
    anti_join(
      prompt_r,
      by = c("File_ID" = "child_id", "clinical_group")
    )

  bind_rows(real_r, syn_r)
})) %>%
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = c("real", "synthetic")),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI")),
    source_is_synthetic = if_else(source == "synthetic", 1L, 0L),
    age_cohort = factor(
      age_cohort,
      levels = c("4_year_old", "5_year_old", "6_year_old", "7_year_old")
    ),
    cluster_id = if_else(
      source == "synthetic",
      paste0("synthetic_", age_cohort, "_", round_id, "_", pair_id),
      paste0("real_", File_ID)
    ),
    Age_c = Age_Month - mean(Age_Month, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(past_overgeneralization_errors),
    !is.na(past_verb_opportunities),
    past_verb_opportunities > 0
  )

df_dev_all_clean <- df_dev_all %>%
  filter(
    past_verb_opportunities > 0,
    past_overgeneralization_errors >= 0,
    past_overgeneralization_errors <= past_verb_opportunities
  )
df_dev_all_clean <- df_dev_all_clean %>%
  mutate(Age_z = as.numeric(scale(Age_Month)))

# Quick checks
table(df_dev_all_clean$source, df_dev_all_clean$clinical_group)
table(df_dev_all_clean$age_cohort, df_dev_all_clean$source, df_dev_all_clean$clinical_group)
summary(df_dev_all_clean$past_overgeneralization_errors)
summary(df_dev_all_clean$past_verb_opportunities)

```

is age linear or quadratic?
```{r}
library(lme4)

m_age0_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(
    past_overgeneralization_errors,
    past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors
  ) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group +
    (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

m_age1_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(
    past_overgeneralization_errors,
    past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors
  ) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group +
    Age_c +
    (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

m_age2_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(
    past_overgeneralization_errors,
    past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors
  ) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group +
    Age_c + I(Age_c^2) +
    (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
)

anova(m_age0_overgen, m_age1_overgen, m_age2_overgen, test = "Chisq")
AIC(m_age0_overgen, m_age1_overgen, m_age2_overgen)
BIC(m_age0_overgen, m_age1_overgen, m_age2_overgen)
```

```{r}
m0_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(past_overgeneralization_errors,
        past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group  + (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
) # Does the probability of past overgeneralization differ by source (real vs synthetic), by clinical group (TD vs SLI), and by the source-by-group combination, after controlling for round and repeated observations?

m1_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(past_overgeneralization_errors,
        past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group + Age_c  + (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
) # Does the probability of past overgeneralization change with age overall?

m2_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(past_overgeneralization_errors,
        past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group + Age_c +
    source_is_synthetic:Age_c + clinical_group:Age_c +
     + (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
) # Do real and synthetic data show different age slopes, or do TD and SLI show different age slopes?

m3_overgen <- glmer(
  cbind(past_overgeneralization_errors,
        past_verb_opportunities - past_overgeneralization_errors) ~
    source_is_synthetic * clinical_group * Age_c +
     + (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_dev_all_clean,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
) # Is the developmental pattern of past overgeneralization across age and clinical group reproduced differently in synthetic versus real data?

anova(m0_overgen, m1_overgen, m2_overgen, m3_overgen, test = "Chisq")
```
```{r}
summary(m3_overgen) # Does the developmental pattern across age differ jointly by source and clinical group?
```
At mean age, real and synthetic data are fairly similar in overall past-overgeneralization rate, but they differ sharply in how that rate changes with age.

* real TD lower overgeneralisation probability than SLI
* synthetic vs real TD and synthetic vs real SLI not significantly different at mean age
* real TD probability of continue overgeneralising decreases with age
* real SLI have an almost flat slope or only slightly positive
INTERESTING PART:
* synthetic TD and SLI probability of overgeneralisation INCREASES WITH AGE -> flipped developmental pattern
* synthetic SLI slope is also different from synthetic TD

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# -----------------------------
# Cleaner plot for m3_overgen
# - points = age-binned observed means
# - lines/ribbons = model-predicted probabilities
# -----------------------------

# 1) Add observed rate
plot_df <- df_dev_all_clean %>%
  mutate(
    obs_rate = past_overgeneralization_errors / past_verb_opportunities,
    source_label = factor(
      source_is_synthetic,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Real", "Synthetic")
    ),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI"))
  )

# 2) Create 6-month age bins
plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    age_bin = cut(
      Age_Month,
      breaks = c(48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90, 96),
      right = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  )

# 3) Compute binned observed means
#    Weighted by past opportunities, so rows with more opportunities count more
binned_df <- plot_df %>%
  group_by(clinical_group, source_label, age_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    Age_Month_plot = weighted.mean(Age_Month, w = past_verb_opportunities, na.rm = TRUE),
    obs_rate = sum(past_overgeneralization_errors, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(past_verb_opportunities, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_opp = sum(past_verb_opportunities, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4) Prediction grid from m3_overgen
age_grid <- seq(
  min(df_dev_all_clean$Age_c, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(df_dev_all_clean$Age_c, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 150
)

newdat <- expand.grid(
  Age_c = age_grid,
  source_is_synthetic = c(0, 1),
  clinical_group = c("TD", "SLI")
) %>%
  mutate(
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = levels(df_dev_all_clean$clinical_group)),
    source_is_synthetic = as.integer(source_is_synthetic)
  )

X <- model.matrix(
  ~ source_is_synthetic * clinical_group * Age_c,
  data = newdat
)

beta <- lme4::fixef(m3_overgen)
V <- as.matrix(vcov(m3_overgen))

eta <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)
se_eta <- sqrt(diag(X %*% V %*% t(X)))

newdat <- newdat %>%
  mutate(
    Age_Month_plot = Age_c + mean(df_dev_all_clean$Age_Month, na.rm = TRUE),
    fit_link = eta,
    lower_link = eta - 1.96 * se_eta,
    upper_link = eta + 1.96 * se_eta,
    fit = plogis(fit_link),
    lower = plogis(lower_link),
    upper = plogis(upper_link),
    source_label = factor(
      source_is_synthetic,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("Real", "Synthetic")
    ),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group, levels = c("TD", "SLI"))
  )

# 5) Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = newdat,
    aes(
      x = Age_Month_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      fill = source_label
    ),
    alpha = 0.14,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = newdat,
    aes(
      x = Age_Month_plot,
      y = fit,
      color = source_label
    ),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = binned_df,
    aes(
      x = Age_Month_plot,
      y = obs_rate,
      color = source_label,
      size = total_opp
    ),
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ clinical_group, nrow = 1) +
  scale_size_area(
    max_size = 8,
    breaks = c(25, 50, 100, 200),
    labels = c("25", "50", "100", "200")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (months)",
    y = "Past overgeneralization rate",
    color = "Source",
    fill = "Source",
    size = "Past opportunities\n(within bin)",
    title = "Past overgeneralization across age",
    subtitle = "Points are weighted age-binned observed rates; lines are model-predicted probabilities"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

the developmental pattern of bare marking errors is different across the four groups, not just in level but in trajectory.
* at mean age td has a very low bare-marking error rate
* synthetic td is higher than real td
* real sli is higher than td
* synthetic sli much higher

SYNTHETIC DATA INFLATE BARE MARKING ERRORS ESPECIALLY FOR SLI

* no effect of age for td = number of error stays low and costant
* sli errors increase with age (not a worsening of condition but more opportunities probably)
* synthetic sli errors decrease considerably with age

SYNTHETIC DATA PRODUCE THE WRONG DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORY

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# Adjusted means from the retained model
emm_agr <- emmeans(
  m0_agr,
  ~ source_is_synthetic * clinical_group,
  at = list(source_is_synthetic = c(0, 1))
)

emm_agr_df <- as.data.frame(emm_agr) %>%
  mutate(
    population = factor(
      paste(ifelse(source_is_synthetic == 1, "Synthetic", "Real"), clinical_group),
      levels = c("Real TD", "Synthetic TD", "Real SLI", "Synthetic SLI")
    )
  )

# Raw data
df_plot <- df_all %>%
  mutate(
    population = factor(
      paste(ifelse(source_is_synthetic == 1, "Synthetic", "Real"), clinical_group),
      levels = c("Real TD", "Synthetic TD", "Real SLI", "Synthetic SLI")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(agreement_errors_per_finite_verb), !is.na(population))

# Plot
ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = population, y = agreement_errors_per_finite_verb, color = population)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.45, alpha = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.10, alpha = 0.22, size = 1.7) +
  geom_pointrange(
    data = emm_agr_df,
    aes(x = population, y = emmean, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Agreement errors per finite verb"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
The synthetic data inflate morphosyntactic error rates, and the inflation is especially strong for SLI.

```{r}
    source_is_synthetic:ns(Age_Month, df = 3) +
    clinical_group:ns(Age_Month, df = 3) +
    ns(Age_Month, df = 3) +
    (1 | cluster_id),
  data = df_all, REML = FALSE
)

AIC(m_lin_int, m_spline_int)
BIC(m_lin_int, m_spline_int)
```

In the real data, children with SLI produce subjects in a much smaller proportion of utterances than TD children—about 30 percentage points lower at mean age. Subject use increases with age in both groups, but the increase is steeper in SLI, suggesting some developmental catch-up. In the synthetic data, subject use is inflated especially for SLI: synthetic SLI transcripts contain far more subject-bearing utterances than real SLI transcripts, which substantially reduces the real TD–SLI gap.


# Summary

The clearest high-level conclusion is that the synthetic data do not fail in just one way. They show different distortions for different linguistic domains. On broad productivity, synthetic transcripts are more verbose or denser in some respects: MLU is higher in synthetic than real, SLI is lower than TD, and age increases MLU, but the TD–SLI separation is broadly preserved.  On lexical diversity, though, the distortion is much stronger: real SLI is much lower than real TD, but synthetic SLI is pushed up to the same level as synthetic TD, effectively flattening a clinically meaningful difference. 
For developmental grammar, DSS tells a different story from VOCD-D. Synthetic transcripts are slightly lower than real ones on DSS, SLI is lower than TD, and DSS increases with age; the source-by-group interaction is only weak, so the TD–SLI difference is still broadly preserved. That means the synthetic data do not simply look globally “better” or “worse” than real data. They look richer on some measures and poorer on others. 
The productive-morphology results are especially informative. Past overgeneralization is rare overall, as expected in spontaneous speech, but it is pushed almost to floor in the synthetic data, especially for TD, and the age-by-group pattern differs between real and synthetic transcripts. In other words, the generator underproduces a normal developmental error pattern rather than reproducing it faithfully.  By contrast, nonfiniteness-related error measures go in the opposite direction: bare-marking errors and agreement errors are both much higher in the synthetic data, especially for synthetic SLI, suggesting that the generator overcreates morphosyntactic errorfulness in that group.  Determiner usage per utterance also shows a strong distortion: real SLI uses determiners much less than real TD, but synthetic SLI is boosted upward, partially narrowing the real clinical gap. 
The syntax results are more mixed, but again interpretable. Mean tree depth and complex NP proportion are both higher in synthetic than real transcripts, while SLI remains lower than TD; there is no strong interaction, so the basic group ordering is preserved even though the synthetic data are structurally denser overall.  Subordination behaves more conservatively: SLI is lower than TD, subordination increases with age, and there is no strong real-versus-synthetic difference.  So the synthetic data seem to increase structural depth more than they increase developmentally appropriate syntax.
If I had to reduce the whole PDF to one thesis sentence, it would be this:
The synthetic transcripts often preserve broad developmental ordering, but they do not preserve the linguistic profile faithfully: they inflate lexical richness and structural density, suppress normal developmental error patterns like past overgeneralization, and exaggerate morphosyntactic error rates—especially in SLI.

Take-home points:


first, measures where synthetic data mostly preserve the real group structure while shifting level: MLU, DSS, mean tree depth, complex NP proportion


second, measures where synthetic data distort clinically meaningful contrasts: VOCD-D, determiner usage


third, error-pattern measures showing opposite failures: past overgeneralization too low, bare/agreement errors too high, especially in synthetic SLI.


A strong discussion paragraph could be built around the contrast between “deeper syntax without better grammar” and “richer vocabulary without realistic clinical separation.”


```{r}
# ============================================================
# Compact univariate feature-summary plot
# Synthetic-real shift by clinical group
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Choose features for the presentation plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

feature_lookup <- tibble::tribble(
  ~feature,                          ~label,                       ~domain,
  "MLU_Morphemes",                   "MLU",                        "Broad structure",
  "DSS_tbl_score",                   "DSS",                        "Broad structure",
  "VOCD_D_optimum_average",          "Lexical diversity",          "Lexicon",
  "Syntax_Mean_TreeDepth",           "Mean tree depth",            "Syntax",
  "Syntax_ComplexNP_Utt_Prop",       "Complex NP proportion",      "Syntax",
  "Syntax_AuxCop_Utt_Prop",          "Aux/Cop proportion",         "Morphosyntax",
  "bare_marking_errors_per_word",    "Bare marking errors",        "Errors",
  "agreement_errors_per_finite_verb", "Agreement errors",          "Errors"
)

# Keep only features that exist in df_all
feature_lookup <- feature_lookup %>%
  filter(feature %in% names(df_all))

if (nrow(feature_lookup) == 0) {
  stop("None of the selected feature columns exist in df_all.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Prepare long dataframe and standardise each feature
# ------------------------------------------------------------

analysis_long <- df_all %>%
  mutate(
    source_eval = case_when(
      source_is_synthetic == 0 ~ "real",
      source_is_synthetic == 1 ~ "synthetic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    source_eval = factor(source_eval, levels = c("real", "synthetic")),
    clinical_group = factor(clinical_group),
    cluster_id = factor(cluster_id)
  ) %>%
  select(
    File_ID,
    source,
    source_eval,
    clinical_group,
    Age_c,
    cluster_id,
    all_of(feature_lookup$feature)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(feature_lookup$feature),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  left_join(feature_lookup, by = "feature") %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(value),
    !is.na(source_eval),
    !is.na(clinical_group),
    !is.na(Age_c),
    !is.na(cluster_id)
  ) %>%
  group_by(feature) %>%
  mutate(
    real_mean = mean(value[source_eval == "real"], na.rm = TRUE),
    real_sd   = sd(value[source_eval == "real"], na.rm = TRUE),
    value_z   = if_else(
      !is.na(real_sd) & real_sd > 0,
      (value - real_mean) / real_sd,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is.finite(value_z))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit one mixed model per feature
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_one_feature <- function(dat) {
  tryCatch(
    lmer(
      value_z ~ source_eval * clinical_group + Age_c + (1 | cluster_id),
      data = dat,
      REML = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Model failed: ", e$message)
      NULL
    }
  )
}

models <- analysis_long %>%
  group_by(feature, label, domain) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(model = map(data, fit_one_feature)) %>%
  filter(!map_lgl(model, is.null))

if (nrow(models) == 0) {
  stop("No models were successfully fitted.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Extract synthetic-real contrasts within each clinical group
# ------------------------------------------------------------

extract_source_contrasts <- function(model) {

  emm <- emmeans(
    model,
    ~ source_eval | clinical_group
  )

  # synthetic - real because source_eval levels are real, synthetic
  con <- contrast(
    emm,
    method = list("synthetic - real" = c(-1, 1))
  )

  # p-values / test statistics
  con_sum <- summary(con) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  # confidence intervals
  con_ci <- confint(con) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  # Robust CI naming across emmeans versions
  if ("lower.CL" %in% names(con_ci)) {
    con_ci <- con_ci %>%
      rename(lower_ci = lower.CL, upper_ci = upper.CL)
  } else if ("asymp.LCL" %in% names(con_ci)) {
    con_ci <- con_ci %>%
      rename(lower_ci = asymp.LCL, upper_ci = asymp.UCL)
  } else if ("lower.HPD" %in% names(con_ci)) {
    con_ci <- con_ci %>%
      rename(lower_ci = lower.HPD, upper_ci = upper.HPD)
  } else {
    stop("No recognised confidence interval columns found in emmeans output.")
  }

  con_sum %>%
    left_join(
      con_ci %>%
        select(clinical_group, contrast, lower_ci, upper_ci),
      by = c("clinical_group", "contrast")
    )
}

contrast_df <- models %>%
  mutate(contrasts = map(model, extract_source_contrasts)) %>%
  select(feature, label, domain, contrasts) %>%
  unnest(contrasts) %>%
  mutate(
    clinical_group = as.character(clinical_group),
    domain = factor(
      domain,
      levels = c(
        "Broad structure",
        "Lexicon",
        "Syntax",
        "Morphosyntax",
        "Errors"
      )
    ),
    label = factor(label, levels = rev(unique(feature_lookup$label)))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Inspect numerical table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

contrast_table <- contrast_df %>%
  select(
    label,
    domain,
    clinical_group,
    estimate,
    SE,
    df,
    lower_ci,
    upper_ci,
    any_of(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio", "p.value"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(domain, label, clinical_group)

print(contrast_table)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Compact coefficient plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_univariate_summary <- ggplot(
  contrast_df,
  aes(
    x = estimate,
    y = fct_reorder(label, estimate),
    xmin = lower_ci,
    xmax = upper_ci,
    shape = clinical_group
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    height = 0.18,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.55),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.55),
    size = 2.4
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    domain ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y",
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Synthetic − real difference\n(real-data SD units)",
    y = NULL,
    shape = "Group",
    title = "Feature-level synthetic-real shifts",
    subtitle = "Positive values mean synthetic data are higher than real data"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 10
    ),
    strip.text.y.right = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.35, "lines")
  )

p_univariate_summary

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save for Beamer
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create("images", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0("images/icl_univariate_feature_summary", plot_suffix, ".pdf"),
  plot = p_univariate_summary,
  width = 7.4,
  height = 4.8
)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0("images/icl_univariate_feature_summary", plot_suffix, ".png"),
  plot = p_univariate_summary,
  width = 7.4,
  height = 4.8,
  dpi = 300
)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Operator-validity analysis from reconstructed filename parent key
# Stage 2 SLI − Stage 1 TD
# ============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Choose filename column
# ------------------------------------------------------------

file_col <- if ("File_kideval" %in% names(syn)) {
  "File_kideval"
} else {
  "File_ID"
}

cat("Using filename column:", file_col, "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Reconstruct parent key from filename
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Example:
# stage1_td/pair_sli413_td439_rep10_TD_bundle.cha
# stage2_sli/pair_sli413_td439_rep10_SLI_bundle.cha
#
# Parent key:
# pair_sli413_td439_rep10

syn_parent <- syn %>%
  mutate(
    file_name = as.character(.data[[file_col]]),
    parent_key = str_extract(
      file_name,
      "pair_sli[0-9]+_td[0-9]+_rep[0-9]+"
    ),
    stage_from_name = case_when(
      str_detect(file_name, "stage1_td") ~ "stage1_td",
      str_detect(file_name, "stage2_sli") ~ "stage2_sli",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Check parsing
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cat("\nParsing check:\n")
print(
  syn_parent %>%
    count(clinical_group, stage_from_name, is.na(parent_key))
)

cat("\nExample parsed filenames:\n")
print(
  syn_parent %>%
    select(clinical_group, file_name, parent_key, stage_from_name) %>%
    group_by(clinical_group) %>%
    slice_head(n = 5) %>%
    ungroup(),
  n = 20
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check whether Stage 2 SLI keys match Stage 1 TD keys
# ------------------------------------------------------------

td_keys <- syn_parent %>%
  filter(clinical_group == "TD") %>%
  pull(parent_key) %>%
  unique()

match_check <- syn_parent %>%
  filter(clinical_group == "SLI") %>%
  summarise(
    n_sli_rows = n(),
    n_sli_with_key = sum(!is.na(parent_key)),
    n_sli_matched_to_td = sum(parent_key %in% td_keys, na.rm = TRUE),
    match_rate = mean(parent_key %in% td_keys, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("\nStage 2 SLI to Stage 1 TD match check:\n")
print(match_check)

if (match_check$match_rate < 0.8) {
  warning(
    "Less than 80% of SLI rows match TD parent keys. ",
    "Inspect file_name and parent_key before interpreting results."
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Select features
# ------------------------------------------------------------

operator_features <- feature_lookup %>%
  filter(feature %in% names(syn_parent), feature %in% names(df_all))

if (nrow(operator_features) == 0) {
  stop("No operator features found in both syn_parent and df_all.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Real-data SDs for scaling
# ------------------------------------------------------------

real_feature_sds <- df_all %>%
  filter(source == "real") %>%
  select(all_of(operator_features$feature)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(feature) %>%
  summarise(
    real_sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(real_sd), real_sd > 0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Prepare Stage 1 TD baselines
# ------------------------------------------------------------

td_long <- syn_parent %>%
  filter(clinical_group == "TD") %>%
  select(
    parent_key,
    td_file_name = file_name,
    all_of(operator_features$feature)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(operator_features$feature),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "td_value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(parent_key), is.finite(td_value))

# Check whether TD parent keys are unique
td_key_check <- td_long %>%
  distinct(parent_key, td_file_name) %>%
  count(parent_key, name = "n_td_files") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_td_files))

cat("\nTD files per parent key:\n")
print(td_key_check %>% count(n_td_files))

if (any(td_key_check$n_td_files > 1)) {
  warning(
    "Some parent keys have more than one TD file. ",
    "The analysis will average TD values within parent_key."
  )
  
  td_long <- td_long %>%
    group_by(parent_key, feature) %>%
    summarise(
      td_value = mean(td_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      td_file_name = paste(unique(td_file_name), collapse = " | "),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Prepare Stage 2 SLI outputs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sli_long <- syn_parent %>%
  filter(clinical_group == "SLI") %>%
  select(
    parent_key,
    sli_file_name = file_name,
    all_of(operator_features$feature)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(operator_features$feature),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "sli_value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(parent_key), is.finite(sli_value))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Join SLI outputs to their Stage 1 TD parent
# ------------------------------------------------------------

paired_operator_long <- sli_long %>%
  inner_join(
    td_long,
    by = c("parent_key", "feature"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  left_join(operator_features, by = "feature") %>%
  left_join(real_feature_sds, by = "feature") %>%
  mutate(
    delta_raw = sli_value - td_value,
    delta_z = delta_raw / real_sd
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(delta_z))

cat("\nMatched operator rows:\n")
print(nrow(paired_operator_long))

cat("\nMatched SLI files:\n")
print(n_distinct(paired_operator_long$sli_file_name))

cat("\nMatched TD parent keys:\n")
print(n_distinct(paired_operator_long$parent_key))

if (nrow(paired_operator_long) == 0) {
  stop("No matched Stage 2 SLI / Stage 1 TD rows. Check parent_key parsing.")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Summarise operator effects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

operator_summary <- paired_operator_long %>%
  group_by(feature, label, domain) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sli_outputs = n_distinct(sli_file_name),
    n_td_parents = n_distinct(parent_key),
    mean_delta_z = mean(delta_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_delta_z = sd(delta_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_delta_z = sd_delta_z / sqrt(n_sli_outputs),
    lower_ci = mean_delta_z - 1.96 * se_delta_z,
    upper_ci = mean_delta_z + 1.96 * se_delta_z,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    domain = factor(
      domain,
      levels = c(
        "Broad structure",
        "Lexicon",
        "Syntax",
        "Morphosyntax",
        "Errors"
      )
    )
  )

print(operator_summary)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_operator <- ggplot(
  operator_summary,
  aes(
    x = mean_delta_z,
    y = fct_reorder(label, mean_delta_z),
    xmin = lower_ci,
    xmax = upper_ci
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    height = 0.18,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_grid(
    domain ~ .,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y",
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Stage 2 SLI − Stage 1 TD\n(real-data SD units)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Operator validity of the synthetic SLI transformation",
    subtitle = "Positive values mean Stage 2 increased the feature relative to its Stage 1 TD parent"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      angle = 0,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 10
    ),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0.35, "lines")
  )

p_operator


```
